name: Spatial smoothing of the per-Gaussian statistics (the spatial kernel of BKI): read-out candidates selected on validation, Replica and ScanNet
status: Registered 2026-10-21 (lead decisions D1-D5 of 2026-10-21 applied), before any real-data run: no smoothed row had run on any real scene (validation or test); only CPU toy tests (tests/test_smoothing.py) and a synthetic kNN/pooling benchmark had run. scripts/smooth_tab1.sh refuses every stage while this file is untracked or has uncommitted changes.
amended: 2026-10-21, after the first validation attempt crashed and before any validation number existed (no batch record finished; only the error was read): kernel weights below 1e-12 (a neighbour beyond 7.4 sigma) are set to 0 (usplat.smoothing.W_MIN). Their denormal float32 products made the averaging_s feature's norm underflow (feature = inf) on 3 of 620,290 Gaussians of Replica office_0 (isolated, unseen Gaussians), and eval_seg refused the buffer. The change alters every pooled sum by less than 1e-12 of a neighbour's evidence; nothing else in this file changed.

code.rows: usplat/smoothing.py (row factory usplat.smoothing:row_factory; GRID and batches() must equal 'candidates' and 'batches' below: tests/test_smoothing.py)
code.selection: scripts/smooth_select.py (select, check-test, table, claim; reuses scripts/make_tables.py choose_v2 / pooled / check_code and scripts/quant_stats.py sign_test / holm)
code.factories: usplat.baselines:row_factory,usplat.smoothing:row_factory (the unsmoothed averaging row comes from the Table I code path)

after: A later attempt, after Table I (v1 and v2) was final: Table I shows ours tied with averaging (Replica mIoU 28.0 vs 27.9, ScanNet 68.0 vs 67.7). The idea (BKI pools observations over space as well as over views; our field pools over views only) was chosen before any smoothed number existed; no smoothed row was evaluated on any scene before this file was committed.
maps: The existing Table I maps and fields (Replica: uags_fields/<scene>_lseg.pt on uags_maps/<scene>_seq1.pt; ScanNet: uags_fields/scannet/<scene>_lseg.pt on uags_maps/scannet/<scene>.pt). No re-mapping, no distillation: every new row is a read-out of the saved field statistics and the saved averaging sums (ckpt['baselines'], NormLift's F and S1), with the Gaussian centres of the field's own map (ckpt config.ply / inputs.ply, checked against the scenes file and field.N).

method.kernel: k_nm = exp(-||x_n - x_m||^2 / (2 sigma^2)) * gate_nm for m among the k nearest OTHER centres of n (kNN by scipy cKDTree, exact), k_nn = 1; sigma = s h, h = median over the scene's Gaussians of the distance to the nearest other centre; weights below 1e-12 are set to 0 (float32 underflow guard, see 'amended')
method.gate: none, or 1[cos(d_n, d_m) >= g] with d the UNSMOOTHED direction of the row's own method (ours: mu*; averaging: its unit feature); a pair where either Gaussian has no evidence (W1 = 0, resp. S1 = 0) passes
method.ours: R' = R + S k R_m, W1' = W1 + S k W1_m, Wr' = Wr + S k Wr_m, W2' = W2 + S k^2 W2_m, Q' = Q + S k^2 Q_m (neighbour views enter with view weight k omega); every read-out is the field's own code on the pooled sums: mu*' = R'/||R'||, u_epi' = 1/(1 + W1'), u_ale' = 1 - rho' (Eq. rho on the pooled sums, defined once W1' >= tau_min = 3)
method.rows: ours_P0s_<tag>: P0 on the pooled sums, one temperature; ours_P2s_<tag>: the same buffer with the P2 temperature beta0 exp(-gamma_e u_epi' - gamma_a u_ale' - gamma_u 1[u_ale' undefined]), all four refit on validation; averaging_s_<tag>: the averaging feature on F' = F + S k F_m, S1' = S1 + S k S1_m, normalised, one temperature
method.uncertainty_channels: u_epi and u_ale of the smoothed rows are RECOMPUTED from the pooled sums (not smoothed per-Gaussian values). Table I's AUSE_u column of a smoothed row is the AUSE of its own u_ale' (eval_seg ranking signal 'u_ale'); the unsmoothed ours_P2 keeps its own u_ale.
method.known_bias: neighbours seen in the same view are correlated observations; the kernel treats them as independent (as BKI does), so W1' overstates the evidence (u_epi' too low) and rho' is biased up (u_ale' too low). The P2 fit rescales the channels; validation decides whether the read-out helps.

justification: Fixed from first principles before any smoothed number existed; no scene statistic was read to set it.

Scale unit h (median nearest-neighbour distance of the scene's centres): the kernel then follows the map's density, which differs between Replica and ScanNet maps of the same Gaussian budget (10^6), so one grid serves both datasets.

s: on a locally uniform surface with median NN distance h the point density is rho = ln2 / (pi h^2), so an untruncated kernel collects 2 pi rho sigma^2 = 2 ln2 s^2 effective neighbours: 1.4, 5.5, 22 and 89 for s = 1, 2, 4, 8 (each doubling of sigma quadruples the pooled evidence). s = 0.5 (0.35 neighbours) is nearly the identity, which the unsmoothed ours_P2 already covers.

Upper limit of s: a dense LSeg feature comes from a 16 x 16 pixel patch, about 10 cm at 2 m depth in Replica's 640 x 480 frames (f = 320); a 10^6-Gaussian room has h of the order of 0.5 cm (synthetic 6 x 5 x 3 m room surface with 10^6 points: h = 0.58 cm, measured on CPU), so sigma = 8h is about 4 cm, still inside one patch: the kernel pools evidence of the same feature cell and does not blur detail the extractor resolves. s = 8 was added by the lead's decision D5 (2026-10-21), before any data.

k: the k-th neighbour of a uniform surface lies at about h sqrt(k/ln2) (3.4h, 4.8h, 6.8h for k = 8, 16, 32; 5.8h measured at k = 32 on the synthetic room), where the kernel weight is exp(-k/(2 ln2 s^2)). k = 32 leaves s <= 2 untruncated (<= 0.003) and s = 4 truncated at weight 0.24; at s = 8 every k truncates (weight 0.70 at the 32nd neighbour), so s = 8 is close to a uniform mean over the k nearest neighbours, with k setting its size (8, 16, 32). In 3DGS maps the density varies (clusters of small Gaussians on texture, sparse large ones on flat walls), so k and sigma are not interchangeable there. Expected near-duplicates: at s = 1 the three k give almost the same kernel (weights <= 0.003 beyond the 8th neighbour); the tie rule then keeps the smallest k.

g: none = the plain BKI spatial kernel. 0.8 blocks neighbours whose unsmoothed directions differ by more than 37 degrees, a guard against pooling across object boundaries that leaves same-object neighbours (cosines near 1) untouched. In the uncentred PCA-64 LSeg space features of different objects share a large common component, so the gate may block few pairs; this was not measured (no data was read) and is reported with the results (fraction of gated pairs per scene, logged by the factory - see open question in the stage-1 note).
Size: 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 candidates per dataset, the same 24 for both datasets, plus the unsmoothed ours_P2.
grid.order: list order = tie order, least smoothing first: s ascending, then k ascending, then gated before ungated

batch_rule: one eval_seg run per batch (one sigma): rows = the reference rows ours_P0, ours_P2, averaging plus ours_P0s/ours_P2s/averaging_s of the batch's 6 candidates (eval_seg --rows). The reference rows are in every batch: their validation betas and per-scene metrics must agree across the batch records within consistency_tol (scripts/smooth_select.py select refuses otherwise), so the batches act as one evaluation.

replica.test_look: a FURTHER look at the Replica test split: earlier looks were Table I v1, the views test (and the room_0 repeat), the Table IV ablations, Table I v2 (the second look of tab1_v2_prereg.json) and the qualitative render (quant_review.md section 1h)

scannet.test_look: the SECOND look at the ScanNet test split: the first was Table I v1 + v2 in one run (2026-10-19/20, scannet_tab1/look_test.json)

metric.name: nll
metric.text: validation NLL in nats with the coverage rule (variant 'all'), pooled over the labelled pixels of the dataset's validation scenes: sum_s n_s NLL_s / sum_s n_s; temperatures fit by eval_seg.py on the same validation scenes (one fit per row, P2 parameters for the adaptive rows)

tie.rule: candidates within tol nats of the lowest value tie; the tie goes to the one listed first. @smooth lists the unsmoothed ours_P2 first, so a smoothed row must beat it by more than tol; then the grid order (least smoothing first).

@smooth.text: per dataset: the row of Table I's ours P2 line. If it is ours_P2, smoothing is not selected on that dataset: Table I keeps ours_P2 and every smoothed row is reported as not selected.

@avg_own.text: per dataset: averaging with ITS OWN validation-best kernel (lowest pooled validation NLL among averaging and the 24 averaging_s, averaging first) - the strongest fair smoothed averaging; binding in claim rule C1 (decision D1).

paired_baseline: averaging_s with the SAME kernel as @smooth (averaging_s_<tag of @smooth>); none when @smooth is ours_P2. Both averaging_s rows are fit and evaluated like every row; the kernel of averaging_s_<@smooth> is never chosen on averaging's own numbers.
reporting: Every candidate (ours_P0s, ours_P2s, averaging_s of all 24 kernels) and the reference rows are evaluated on validation and test and reported (appendix), selected or not; test numbers of rows not selected are labelled 'not selected'.

Table I: if @smooth is a smoothed row on a dataset, the paper adds the rows 'Ours P2, spatial kernel' (mIoU and accuracy of ours_P0s of the same kernel, the other columns of ours_P2s), 'Averaging, same kernel' (averaging_s of that kernel) and 'Averaging, own kernel' (@avg_own) for that dataset, with the AUSE_u of ours_P2s's own u_ale'; the v1 rows are not changed.
Also reported (descriptive, unadjusted, x/N): ours_P2s vs the unsmoothed ours_P2 on each Table I metric, per dataset; the fraction of kNN pairs blocked by the gate and h per scene (factory log).
The selection is final once STAGE=test starts: test numbers never change a choice, the grid, the tie rule, the claim rule or this file.
The test split of each dataset is evaluated once per batch (a crashed batch may be rerun with the same selection; a finished batch never).

claim.C1_gain: The paper may write that the spatial kernel makes ours better than averaging on a Table I metric M (mIoU via ours_P0s, ECE, NLL, Brier, AURC via ours_P2s) on dataset D only if, on the test scenes of D, the chosen smoothed row has a better mean than EACH of averaging, averaging_s with the same kernel, and averaging_s with its own kernel (@avg_own; decision D1), AND is better in more than half of the D test scenes against each of them (x/N >= 4/6 Replica, >= 5/8 ScanNet; a tie is not a win). Otherwise the text says 'on par with averaging' (or worse, as measured).
claim.C2_significance: 'Significantly' only if, in addition, the exact two-sided sign test (ties dropped) over the pooled test scenes of the datasets where @smooth selected a smoothed row gives a Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 within family F3s, and C1 holds on each of those datasets.

F3s.tests: ours (smoothed) vs {averaging, averaging_s same kernel, averaging_s own kernel} x {miou, ece, nll, brier, aurc}: 15 sign tests, Holm over the 15
F3s.scenes: pooled over the test scenes of the datasets where @smooth is a smoothed row (14 if both, 6 or 8 if one; with one dataset alone no test can reach Holm p < 0.05: the smallest sign p is 0.031 (N = 6) or 0.0078 (N = 8), times 15)
F3s.difference: per scene, positive = ours better, in the metric's own unit (configs/quant_prereg.json F1 conventions: points x100, nats for NLL)
F3s.declared_in: this file (configs/quant_prereg.json family F3: 'package-2 claims, each declared in its own prereg before it runs')

claim.calibration: configs/quant_prereg.json R2 applies: a calibration difference (ECE, NLL, Brier) is written only if it has the same sign under the scene mean and the pixel-pooled aggregation, in addition to C1.

disclosure: Paper sentence (Setup or the Table I paragraph): 'After Table I was final we tried one more read-out, a spatial kernel that pools each Gaussian's statistics with its k nearest neighbours (as in BKI); its kernel was chosen per dataset by validation NLL among 24 candidates fixed in advance and the unsmoothed P2, and the test scenes were scored once with that choice (Replica: a further look at its test split; ScanNet: the second); every candidate is in the appendix.' If @smooth is ours_P2 on both datasets: 'A spatial kernel ... did not beat P2 on validation (appendix).'

gpu.basis: per batch at N = 1e6: frozen buffers 3 reference rows (mu* shared by ours_P0/P2, averaging: 0.5 GB) + 6 candidates x (P0s/P2s buffer + averaging_s buffer: 0.5 GB) = 3.5 GB, plus the render workspace measured in Table I v1 (2.51 GiB peak with about 2.0 GB of frozen buffers, eval_test_224fe1e.json) ~0.5 GB: ~4.0 GB peak allocated; cap 6000 MiB (1.5x). 4 batches per stage (one per s). The first batch's record (memory.peak_gpu_alloc_gib) is checked before the next ones.

decisions: D1 (lead, 2026-10-21): @avg_own (averaging at its own best validation kernel) is binding in claim rule C1, next to averaging and averaging_s with ours' kernel.
D2: the gate g = 0.8 stays a candidate next to g = none; selection decides; the factory logs the share of pairs the gate blocks.
D3: both datasets (Replica and ScanNet) are run; the paper discloses the extra test looks.
D4: h per scene (each scene's own median nearest-neighbour distance).
D5: the scale grid is extended to s in {1, 2, 4, 8} (sigma up to about 4 cm, still inside one LSeg patch): 24 candidates per dataset, 4 batches. Decided before any data.
